doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Leaving the Air Force for New York
summary: Out of the Air Force, he was urged by Woody Herman saxophonist Bob Newman to go to New York, but Newman had left by the time he arrived; he stayed fifteen years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I guess you did. When I look at the list of people that you’ve played with and that have played with you it’s pretty darn impressive. You eventually, like a lot of people, moved to New York. Was that specifically for the music?

Yeah it sure was. I had just come out of the Air Force. I had spent two years in the Air Force and I was deciding which coast to go to. I knew I wasn’t going home to the Twin Cities. But I was going to go to either New York or California. And I ran into, well I was stationed in Salt Lake. And the Woody Herman band came through. I met some guys on that band and hung out with them for the couple days they were in town. And they encouraged me. And one of them was Bob Newman, a saxophone player. He encouraged me to come to York. He says, “You’ve got to go to New York, that’s where it’s really happening, that’s where the most creatives are,” he says, “that’s where Sonny Rollins is.” “Oh,” I said. Then I understood. Of course I’ve got to go to New York. Well it turns out I did go to New York. And Bob of course said, “As soon as you get there, look me up, I can get you work right away.” Wouldn’t you know it, when I got there, a few months later, Bob was nowhere to be found. He had left New York by that time. So that was it. And I stayed in New York for fifteen years or so and played a lot. I mean I didn’t lack for work and got to play with just about all the good musicians I ever dreamed of playing with. But I never met or got to play with Sonny Rollins. I saw him in person a couple of times, yeah, but I don’t think I ever did have the pleasure of meeting him.
